response_text: Yielding and time-based pre-emptive context switching can work together because they complement each other: yielding allows tasks to voluntarily give up the CPU when they finish or reach a logical pause point, while the timer-based pre-emptive mechanism ensures that no task can hog the CPU indefinitely. When a task calls osYield(), it explicitly signals the scheduler to switch to another task, enabling cooperative multitasking. Meanwhile, the timer interrupt triggers a PendSV exception at regular intervals, forcing the OS to pre-empt the running task and switch context if its time slice expires. By combining these, the system benefits from efficient voluntary context switches while still maintaining fairness and responsiveness through forced, time-driven pre-emption—so even if a task never yields, the timer ensures other tasks still get CPU time.\n
